utterances.text: From your statement it seems that you observed a door in front of the hangar. Do you know how many doors, entrances there were to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two, one next to another or one front and back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One front, one back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one could you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see inside, and how far inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you could see because the door was open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was daytime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any light inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since now you use your full first and last name, I do not have your date of birth. Can you give us that information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you need to know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Because you were in Valjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to the date of birth. I do not see that that is relevant. I think it is trying to get too much identification information from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I apologise. I think that he only asked for his face protection measure, but if he refuses to answer any questions, that is fine, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if Mr. Fila can explain the relevance of this, but broadcasting this man's date of birth to everyone in the world -- just do not see the reason for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: On the other hand, we have his name, I mean, so I wonder... Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: My next question would be the date of birth, the names of father and mother and his nationality. That is what you have in every statement and there is none of that information available in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You may proceed. Yes. Do ask this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So if you could give me your date of birth, where you were born, what is your ethnic background and what is your father and mother's name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not wish to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness why he is refusing to answer this question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because of my safety, simply said. Because I am from Kosovo, this is under the Serbian occupation, so that is why, and I live in Croatia. I have a family in Croatia, but I also have old family in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Are you an Albanian by ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that only the local Vukovar people were fighting in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many such locals from Vukovar were there, like you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ones who fought in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is part of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean Kosovo is Croatia? So are you from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am an Albanian from Croatia. I have the ID, I have the passport, I went to school in Croatia, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the JNA did you take your weapons with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was probably not your property.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was issued to me by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that why you were tried in Belgrade? Is that why you had a trial against you in Belgrade, because you took away a rifle that was not your property?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for desertion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you shoot from that rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement it says that you joined the fighting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did join.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you shoot from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From a rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it that rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was another rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A hunting rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to the rifle that was issued to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I threw it away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am telling you the truth. Before we went to Vukovar we threw away our rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there was no other weapons but hunting rifles, there was no mortars in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see any mortars or rockets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in the police station. Is that near the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 200 metres from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a straight line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On foot, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about in a straight line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not an expert for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you an expert for guns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not. No, I was just in the armoured mechanised unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any weapons at the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just small arms weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see? Hunting rifles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some pistols. There were very few automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And lastly, how many buses were there at Ovcara when you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Six or seven, I am not sure. I know that I was in the last one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You include the bus that you were on in amongst this six or seven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, it is six to seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I have no other questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions. First of all, you said when you were at the barracks you said in your oral testimony that you saw soldiers, volunteers and White Eagles. What do you mean by, "volunteers"? Probably these were not members of JNA. Were they paramilitary people? Paramilitary troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was -- these were their paramilitary troops. There were civilians. These were Serb civilians who had put on these Chetnik uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were carrying weapons? Were they carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes they did carry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have two questions relating to the period when you were a member of the JNA, around September 1991. First of all, you said that when you were in a unit, a member of the unit which was shelling Vukovar, no distinction was made by your unit between military and civilian objectives, or targets. I wonder whether you were under military instructions, in other words, whether you had received orders to this effect; namely not to distinguish between military and civilian objectives or whether this was an initiative of your unit. Are you aware, were you aware of any orders or instructions issued by superior authorities to the effect that you should not make any distinction between civilian and military objectives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We received instructions from our commander to destroy the town, that there was no distinction between the military and civilian targets. There were no military targets in Vukovar. These were all civilian targets that we were shelling, so that anything that was Croatian would be destroyed, mildly said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said again that when you were a member of this unit of the JNA you were -- and I am quoting your words, you were, "closely co-operating with paramilitary troops". Could you explain what you mean by, "close co-operation", with the paramilitary troops? Close co-operation between members of the JNA and paramilitary troops there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military personnel collaborated with them, the officers did not meet personally. They had the headquarters in Negoslavci and that is where the Arkan's people and Seselj's people and the military, and the White Eagles, that is where they would all meet together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know whether these paramilitary troops were receiving instructions from the JNA or whether they were part of the chain of command in the JNA or whether totally independent, acting independently of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that they acted independently and what it did was just unbelievable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any objection to the witness being released? Thank you so much for coming, Mr. Dodaj. You may now be released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too for having listened to me. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution going to call Witness I?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, this witness has sort of turned the other way around and he has agreed that he is called by his own name. He just wishes, like the previous witness, not his face being shown. (The witness entered court) (3.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. May I ask you to make the solemn declaration? ZLATKO ZLOGLEDA (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Prosecutor, you may proceed. Examined by MR. WAESPI

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. Good afternoon, Mr. Zlogleda.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the record, can you please state your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zlatko Zlogleda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you interviewed in April 1996 by an investigator from this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall having signed a document which was the English translation of that interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I please ask the usher, as soon as he has finished his previous job... thank you. (Handed). Can you please have a look at this document and tell us whether you find your signature at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like the usher again to show it to the Defence, and tender it into evidence as I assume, exhibit number 25 as of the English document and 25A as of the Croatian translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No objection to that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So, let us start with the examination. Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sisak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is in Croatia, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please outline for us your educational background and your work experience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I finished elementary school in Hrvatska Dubica and secondary school in Bosanka Dubica and I was not employed after I finished school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After school did you then go straight into the army? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which army is that? Is that the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Valjevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but by, "army", we agree that is the JNA.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the JNA, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long have you been in this army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us exactly in what time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From March until September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are talking about 1991, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you outline to us what kind of military service did you do? Did you first start with the training? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We had accelerated training for about three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After having completed this training, were you told to go now to some place, to resume your duties as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when we finished this shorter training we were supposed to go to Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever reach Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We reached Sabac and that is where we stayed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you stay in Sabac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed there about two months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, thereafter were you told to do something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They said that the situation was quiet now, that we would be going back to barracks either in Sabac or Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which barracks did you go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not go to any barracks. We stayed in Sabac, the same place where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this stay in Sabac, were you supposed to go to Vukovar? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We left Sabac for Vukovar and Sid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you arrive first in Vukovar or first in Sid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. First to Sid and then from Sid we went to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you go directly into the town or did you have to hold some positions outside the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We came to Negoslavci and from Negoslavci we were in the suburbs of Vukovar, not in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point did you decide to escape, to desert?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall what date that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That was around 20th September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is still 1991?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to us why did you decide to escape? Were you encouraged by the fact that the ethnic composition of the JNA was mostly Serbian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Because everything showed that this was a Serbian army. The flag, the Serbian songs, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Serbian soldiers who served with you also tell you that you should leave the army because it is now a Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They kept provoking us. They said, "what are you waiting for Ustashas, ZNGs, why are not you running away"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you ran away. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to, exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Went to our settlement called Luzac, I think, and then with the assistance of a civilian we got to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where exactly did you go in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Went to the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eventually join a Croatian formation now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how this formation was called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reserve composition of the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also go to the front-line now with this unit you have just described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We went to a front-line, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eventually go to the Vukovar hospital because one of the persons who was with you was injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We took this person to the hospital and we remained in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the date when you went to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was 18th November 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the hospital, did you see any JNA soldiers, your former comrades and reservists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day when we arrived, no, not yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next day, that is to say some time on the 19th in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of soldiers were they? Can you describe them to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were the local Serbs, reservists who were full of hatred, despair, I do not know what. They looked terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you tell what the difference was between those local Serbs and the JNA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Basically there was not any difference, but these local reservists were even more unkempt than the JNA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, when you were in the hospital, was there still the battle going on in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Practically there was no more fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is to say I stayed that day until the next morning and during the night too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you staying in the hospital on a certain floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not really understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a basement in the hospital where you were staying, or were you on the first or second floor in the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was in the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told that the people in the hospital would be evacuated ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is to say that in the afternoon of 19th there was an evacuation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also evacuated in the course of this evacuation you just described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That is when they evacuated old people, women and children. I decided to stay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, turn to go the next morning, the morning of 20th November, were you told to go towards the exit of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was around 8 o'clock in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you saw at the entrance? People, vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the entrance there were Serb soldiers, reservists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened with you? Were you directed to behave in a certain way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were told to put our hands on our backs and to go out of the hospital and to line up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These Serb soldiers searched us, and we had to stand there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they search you for? Do you have an idea?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were searching us in order to find some weapons or something, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any children or women around you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there were a few women and that they were medical staff but I did not see any children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the women searched as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened next? Were you taken to buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When all of that was over we were told that we should board the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many buses were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my estimate, about eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe those buses? Were they civilians or military buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these were civilian buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall the colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think blue and red .

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going back for a moment to the soldiers who were searching you. Were they also local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they also point at some of the men who were then removed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They would recognise their friends, their neighbours, and they would get them out of the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you see only soldiers around there or also an officer with a rank ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he the only ranking officer being there, at least what you saw personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him and I recognised him, but I think there were other officers too with a lower rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What impression did you have of Sljivancanin? Did you think he was in charge there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Sljivancanin part of the JNA or part of the local Serbs you described a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: JNA. All of them are basically the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw local Serbs, you saw also Sljivancanin being part of the JNA; were there also JNA soldiers there, around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the impression that all the soldiers, JNA, but also the local ones, acted in concert?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw about Sljivancanin, how long were you able to see him there around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He passed by a few times. He would go into the hospital and get out of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, taking into account the search and everything, about an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you were taken to the buses, you just described a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there guards on your bus ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a driver who was armed and I think two more men up there near the driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the driver also wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He had a uniform too, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, those guards, were they from the JNA or local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guards I think were JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were on the bus with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The bus was full.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And "full", means about how many people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, between 40 and 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know one of the other passengers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dodaj Hajdar, and I do not remember the other names. I remember their faces more than their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told where the trip in this bus went to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They simply set off and we were moving in an unknown direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you pulled off with those buses did you have the impression that the fighting in the city still was going on, or had it stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no more fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the trip go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were driving us towards the Vukovar barracks where we stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take to arrive, for you to, at this destination, the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when you arrived at those barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, let us say it was around 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened at the barracks? First of all, did you see any soldiers around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Their soldiers were in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you again tell us whether those were JNA soldiers or soldiers you would describe as local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Again, it was mixed. JNA soldiers and local Serbs and reservists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did local Serbs enter the bus you were sitting in and started to beat people who were sitting in the front of the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They came in through the front door and they were beating people up and they were yelling, shouting, "Ustasha, we are going to kill all of you", and, "all of you are going to be executed".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that these soldiers are local Serbs because neighbours in your buses sort of knew them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because they were getting into the bus and they recognised three or four of them and they got them out of the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So people were taken from the buses. How many in -- with regard to your own bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From my bus they took out about four men, 4-5 men, 5, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we know their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I think three or four were local people from Vukovar and there was a boy from Zagreb. I know that he is from Zagreb but I do not know what his name was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the barracks, in the yard around the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed there for about an hour, perhaps two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we went on further. We did not know where they were taking us and then we stopped in front of a hangar on a field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just getting a minute back, were there still guards on the bus when you took off at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these guards the same ones as had entered the bus in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Maybe that would be a convenient time, your Honours, to stop for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (4.00 pm) (A short break) (4.25 pm)

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just before the break you were mentioning that the buses, again, pulled off into another direction, starting at the barracks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you told this time where the trip would go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did the trip, in fact, go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We started in the direction that we did not know, and then we stopped in front of a hangar in a field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take for you, for your bus to arrive at this destination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 20 minutes to half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said there was a hangar. Can you describe in more detail what you saw there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This was a long building. The door was open, and later the people from the buses entered it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the buses, were there any other vehicles, military, civilian, farming machinery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were military vehicles there, transport vehicles, Jeeps, APCs, and civilian bulldozers. There was one off to the side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which position was your bus with respect to all the other buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in a column. That is, they moved in a column, one behind the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did you think at this point when you arrived this location? What was going to happen? What were your feelings? Can you describe it to us after so many years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I sensed that something would go awry at the time that we got off there, that something was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened to the passengers of the other buses, the ones in front of you? What could you observe from your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. All the buses would stop in front of this door and people were getting off the bus and were supposed to enter the hangar and to the side there were soldiers with batons, sticks, stakes, and they were beating the people who were passing there while entering the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there some people from over sort of walking from the buses to the hangar singled out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were the local Serbs who probably would recognise their neighbours and they would be separated, so they would be also beaten up but would not enter this hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned local Serbs. Were there also JNA solders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers altogether? The local Serbs and the JNA soldiers? Can you give us an indication about the numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about 30 of them altogether, maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether there were more JNA soldiers or more local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there were even little more of the local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after your bus had stopped, did a soldier climb into the bus and ask about Albanians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They entered and they asked whether there were any Albanians there, that they should step forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there any Albanians in your bus that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was Dodaj. He stepped forward and the soldier told him that he would be his.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When our turn came, I think there was a lieutenant colonel or a colonel there with two of his colleagues there who had been beaten and they told him, they told him that they were JNA soldiers, that they had been taken prisoner and then they asked whether there were any additional prisoners and they told them about the two of us, so they waited for us at the door of the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said the two colleagues, those were colleagues of yours and not of the JNA officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Our colleagues who were in the bus before us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name us those two colleagues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Petar Kuscevic and Samir Hrkic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened when you got off the bus? Did you have to go through the same line of beating soldiers as you had described with respect to the other passengers, or were you taken aside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We did not have to pass through. They waited for us and they put us aside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went to your two colleagues and this JNA officer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten as well in the course of these hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the officer you just mentioned look like? I think you said you indicated the rank, like a colonel. Can you describe him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He had greying hair, receding hair, and he was not very tall. And a bit stocky.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give any indication about his age?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 40 and 50 years of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a conversation with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you talking with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He questioned us, what JNA unit we were from, where we had been, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he probably assumed that you were JNA soldiers at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He probably thought that we were Serbs, and that we were their soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he find out at a certain time that this was not true, that you were not Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Then later he asked us what nationality we were and then he found out that we were not Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his reaction when he found out that you were not Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said that we need to know that we were military deserters, that we had escaped, that the military deserters are executed, that we would be executed and that there would be a possibility for us to maybe go to Belgrade and face a court martial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier in your testimony that you saw Sljivancanin in the hospital area. Did you see Sljivancanin again now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I believe so. I think he passed by us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he alone or with others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not alone. He was with another two or three officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing also a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the impression that he was again like in the hospital, in charge of the situation there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the conversation with the JNA officer last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was maybe for up to one hour, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time of waiting, were you able to hear what happened to the persons you mentioned being in the -- inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because there was another bus behind us. They all went through that same procedure, so to speak. They would be beaten as they came off the bus and then they would enter the hangars and in the hangars they were beaten additionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As of those beatings, did you see these beatings or did you hear the beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We saw it and we could also hear the moans and screams.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What impression did you have of the scene at Ovcara farm? Was it chaotic or was it well-organised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was -- you could say rather that it was all organised because they were already waiting there, so they knew the location, this hangar, and everything was prepared for these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next after the conversation was over with the JNA officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then he had told us if we spoke only truth that we would be taken to Belgrade to face a trial, and after this conversation which went on for about one hour, we went in the direction of Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left with, I assume a vehicle, what kind of vehicle was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This was one of their military Jeeps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you left, was it still daytime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We thought that we were going directly to Belgrade. However, we stopped in front of a house. We then learned that this was Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was with you in that military vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The driver. This lieutenant colonel and another soldier who was a guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did at one point this lieutenant colonel ever indicate his name to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I personally do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next when you arrived at this location in Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We got out of the vehicle, we were searched again. They brought out some blindfolds and they blindfolded us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you remained blindfolded for how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were blindfolded we were taken one by one to a basement of this house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we entered this basement we also heard moans because there were people there, and based on the moans, and we could peak from underneath our blindfolds a little bit. We saw that there were some wounded people there because some of them were on stretchers too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived there, yes. They were coming and they would beat us. Also they told us that they would also kill us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the persons who were beating you? You just said you were blindfolded, but was there any indication as to the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most probably they were the locals, maybe from Negoslavci, local Serbs because when we were told that we would be killed, they were the JNA soldiers present. They were telling us that they were responsible for us so that they told them to kill us later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at a certain point in time transferred to another location away from Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed there for a few days, about four days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after this time, after these four days, where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After four days we were taken to Belgrade to the barracks in Topcider.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I turn to Mr. Fila, but before you start, Mr. Fila, may I ask you at the request of the interpreters to ask questions and then to wait for the interpretation into English? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You recognise Colonel Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually major. I do not know what he was at the time. Did he wear anything on his head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On his head? Yes, a hat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was on the hat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you start your military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In March.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take an oath at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a hat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was on that hat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I guess it was a star. I guess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean, "you guess"? Was it or was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the five pointed star JNA or Serbian insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you left the barracks, did you have a flag in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What flag?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the barracks? It was a Yugoslavia flag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where and when did you see a Serb flag being flown in the JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Beyond Sid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Sljivancanin in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Yugoslav flag was no more in use while you were in the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reservists had them. They were flying the Serbian flag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the JNA flag?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see JNA flag flying only Serbian flags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the JNA and the reservists were mixed together, so your inference is your own inference. But did the JNA have a flag before you deserted and what was on it? Was it a red star on it or something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were both of them. They were both the red star and the four Ss.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the JNA at the time of Vukovar had four Ss?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the attack on Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw the four S flag during the attack on Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also spoke about a bulldozer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mention this in a previous statement you gave to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not see a mention of this bulldozer in your statement, but if you saw it, why do you -- did you see it being used at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was just parked there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you saw this hangar, when you saw this building, whatever it was, you saw some machinery, some kind of vehicles, Jeeps, things like that. Did you get an impression that this hangar was occupied by the military, that this is where the military was put up, stationed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it did not look like it was something that they -- there would be accommodations --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not mean accommodations, but you said that there were all these vehicles there. What were they doing there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were waiting for the people who were getting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is, "they"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reservists and the JNA military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were also local Serbs there. How did you recognise -- how did you make a distinction between the paramilitaries, the local Serbs and the JNA? Did you know anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personally, I did not know anyone, but by name, when certain people who were getting off the bus, they would call this person by their name, so that means that they were his neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, were these local Serbs townspeople from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you infer by the way they moved that they were locals, that they knew where they were going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Is there any objection to the witness being released? No objection. Thank you so much for coming. You may be released now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too. Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I wonder whether the Prosecution -- have you got another witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Unfortunately we have not today, your Honours. We have run out and we have been going at a speed much faster than we ever anticipated and we have run right out of witnesses, but we will be ready and tooled-up tomorrow morning to proceed from there on in, but we have just had a temporary run out. But Mr. Williamson was going to address your Honours on that anyway, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, you had asked me previously about the statement of Witness K. During the break I was able to ascertain that this statement, I believe, has already been handed over with the witness's name. This witness had originally requested protective measures and then indicated that he did not wish these. When we spoke with him immediately prior to the commencement of the trial, he had rethought it and said that he would like protective measures again, but they were handed over in the anteroom with his real name so I have written his name down at this time and I can give this to the usher when he returns and there is one copy for the Defence and one for your Honours. You can see the witness's name. If, for some reason, you have not received a statement under this name we can certainly provide one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence has indicated that they have that statement. I believe your Honour should as well, but again, if you do not, if you can let us know and we will be happy to provide it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: In addition, witness 10 which was on the list, Vlado Franjic, will not be testifying so as a result we are going to have to supplement this list with additional witnesses for this week and we will be continuing down -- I think it will cover some of those witnesses for which no statements -- from which no statements have been taken, so in relation to those witnesses we will provide a brief summary as to what their testimony will be about tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So tomorrow morning we will start with witness number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: That is correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: And move on to number 11, and then...

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Number 12, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good. All right. We may now stand in recess until tomorrow morning at 9.15 sharp. (4.50 pm)
